title: The Vulnerability of Language Model Benchmarks: Do They Accurately Reflect True LLM Performance?

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing literature on LLM-as-judge evaluations to demonstrate that language models consistently rate their own outputs higher than those of other models.
Reviewing empirical studies showing that LLM evaluators exhibit a consistent preference for longer, more detailed responses, artificially inflating scores for prolific outputs regardless of quality.

Analyzing the subjective nature of human assessments, highlighting evaluation inconsistencies driven by human heuristics, idiosyncratic preferences, and superficial features like formatting, tone, formality, and text coherence.

Evaluating methodological constraints and systemic biases in benchmark design, including selective task curation, historical resource advantages, and standardized evaluation protocols that distort performance metrics.
Examining how LLM judges can perpetuate, internalize, and amplify spurious correlations and inherent algorithmic biases present in their training data when assessing the outputs of target models.
